description: Butterfly chart of the reasons people who would like a pet do not have one, comparing current owners with people who have no pet, Animal Medicines Australia survey 2025. Based on the Vega population pyramid example.

title.description: The big heading and the smaller line under it. On a phone the words are split into shorter lines.

text.signal: narrow ? ['Cost stops owners; home and', 'lifestyle stop others'] : 'Cost stops owners; home and lifestyle stop others'

subtitle.signal: narrow ? ['Reasons people who would like a pet do not', 'have one, by whether they already own a pet,', '2025 (several reasons could be given)'] : 'Reasons people who would like a pet do not have one, by whether they already own a pet, 2025 (several reasons could be given)'

usermeta.readMe: Vega ignores this box. It holds plain-language notes for the parts of the chart that cannot carry their own "description".

scales.y: Gives each reason its own row, from top to bottom, in the order worked out above.
scales.xLeft: Turns a percentage into a length for the left side. 0% is in the middle and bigger numbers go further left.
scales.xRight: Turns a percentage into a length for the right side. 0% is in the middle and bigger numbers go further right. Both sides use the same numbers, so bar lengths can be compared fairly.

usermeta.codeGuide: Signals set the responsive layout and theme. Data transforms derive values; scales map them to positions and colours; marks draw the chart.
usermeta.readingNote: Housing access can limit ownership even before budgeting begins. Affordability alone cannot remove every obstacle.
usermeta.clickSelection: story-interactions.js pins a main-mark selection in pinnedKey and clears it on an empty-space click. Species hues, quantitative colours, symbol areas and plotted positions retain their meanings.

signals.name: colorAccent
signals.description: Colour: the blue highlight colour, used for the one thing we want you to notice. This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-accent in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorMuted
signals.description: Colour: the dark grey colour of small text: labels, axis words and notes. This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-muted in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorHeading
signals.description: Colour: the dark blue colour of chart titles. This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-heading in css/style.css.

signals.name: fontHeading
signals.description: Font: the fancy title font (DM Serif Display). This is only a backup; the real font comes from --font-heading in css/style.css.

signals.name: fontBody
signals.description: Font: the plain font for all other text (Fira Sans). This is only a backup; the real font comes from --font-body in css/style.css.

signals.name: width
signals.description: How wide the chart is. It starts as the width of the box on the page and updates whenever the browser window is resized.

signals.name: narrow
signals.description: True when the chart is less than 620 pixels wide (for example on a phone). Reason names then move above each row and the headers wrap.

signals.name: centreWidth
signals.description: How wide the middle column is: 320 pixels for the reason names on a computer, just a small gap on a phone (names go above the rows).

signals.name: leftEnd
signals.description: Where the left side ends: the bars for current owners grow leftwards from here.

signals.name: rightStart
signals.description: Where the right side starts: the bars for people without a pet grow rightwards from here.

signals.name: rowHeight
signals.description: How tall each reason row is: taller on a phone to fit the name above the bars.

signals.name: plotHeight
signals.description: How tall the area with the bars is: 17 reasons times the row height.

signals.name: barTop
signals.description: Where each bar starts inside its row (as a fraction of the row): near the top on a computer, under the name on a phone.

signals.name: height
signals.description: Bars only; the reading note wraps in HTML below the SVG.

signals.name: colorBorder
signals.description: Grey baseline mark colour supplied by --color-border in css/style.css.

signals.name: hoverReason
signals.description: Temporary hover focus; mouseout restores the default emphasis.

signals.name: pinnedKey
signals.description: Main-mark selection pinned by a click. Empty chart space clears it; the loader preserves it across responsive redraws.

signals.name: focusReason
signals.description: Pinned selection takes precedence over temporary hover.

data.name: barriers
data.description: The survey numbers: for each reason, the share of current owners and the share of people without a pet who gave it.

transform.description: Reshape the table so each reason is one row, with both groups' percentages next to each other.
Copy the current owners' percentage into a shorter field name, "owners".
Copy the percentage for people without a pet into a shorter field name, "non_owners".
Replace short reason names from the file with full words, for example "Ongoing costs of keeping a pet".
transform.expr: {'Ongoing costs': 'Ongoing costs of keeping a pet', 'Already enough pets/do not want more': 'Already have enough pets', 'Initial costs': 'Initial cost of getting a pet', 'Responsibility': 'Responsibility of looking after a pet', 'Unsuitable home/lifestyle': 'Home or lifestyle is not suitable', 'Uncertain employment/living situation': 'Work or living situation is uncertain', 'Other household members': 'Others in the household do not want one', 'Cannot work from home enough': 'Cannot work from home often enough', 'Previous pet died/not ready': 'Previous pet died, not ready for another', 'Landlord restriction': 'Landlord does not allow pets', 'Buying/adoption process too difficult': 'Buying or adopting is too difficult', 'Wait times too long': 'Wait times are too long', 'Allergies': 'Allergies in the household', 'Body corporate/strata restriction': 'Body corporate or strata does not allow pets', 'Gave away previous pet/not ready': 'Had to give away a previous pet'}[datum.reason] || datum.reason

transform.description: Mark the one row to highlight in blue: "Home or lifestyle is not suitable", the row the note talks about.
Work out the row order: most common reasons first, then "Other reasons" and "No particular reason" last.
transform.expr: datum.reason === 'Other reasons' ? 1000 : datum.reason === 'No particular reason' ? 1001 : -(datum.owners + datum.non_owners)

marks.description: The header above the left side: current owners wanting another pet. Vega stacks a second line below the first, so the first line sits one line height (16px) higher to keep both clear of the top bar.

text.signal: narrow ? ['Current owners', 'wanting another'] : ['Current owners', 'wanting another pet']

marks.description: The header above the right side: people without a pet who want one.

text.signal: narrow ? ['Without a pet,', 'wanting one'] : ['People without a pet', 'who want one']

marks.description: The reason names: in the middle column on a computer, above each row on a phone. The highlighted reason is blue.

fill.signal: (focusReason !== null ? datum.reason === focusReason : datum.emphasis) ? colorAccent : colorBorder

tooltip.signal: {'Reason': datum.label, 'Current owners wanting another pet': datum.owners + '%', 'People without a pet who want one': datum.non_owners + '%'}
